item.title: Elevating Your Life As A Single Woman
item.description: Society and social media are always pressuring women to find that "perfect man." We are told that marriage is the highlight of life, and that happiness centers on a partner. This negatively pushes the idea that in order to be happy, you need a man. As a woman, there is so much more to life. Here are a couple of ways to feel comfortable and complete as a single woman. <p>The post Elevating Your Life As A Single Woman first appeared on Her Campus.</p>

item.title: Scrolling Less, Living More: How College Women Can Manage Screen Time Without Missing Out
item.description: Between TikTok breaks that turn into hour-long spirals and late-night scrolling that steals our sleep, screen time can quietly take control of our college experience. Learning to manage it isn’t about deleting every app, it’s about creating balance, so your phone supports your life instead of distracting you from it. <p>The post Scrolling Less, Living More: How College Women Can Manage Screen Time Without Missing Out first appeared on Her Campus.</p>

item.title: Shackles of Patriarchy Laid Down on Women in the Sports World
item.description: Age-old beliefs of how women should present themselves in this world are deep-rooted in the traditional definition of womanhood. Patriarchy expects women to be fragile and feminine and they should not, at any cost, have their bodies look rough and “manly”. <p>The post Shackles of Patriarchy Laid Down on Women in the Sports World first appeared on Her Campus.</p>

item.title: Eat dear Kanye, Eat dear Eminem
item.description: Tenali fed his coat because it got him into the room. Years later, I get it. This story explores identity, social signals, and how music becomes my “coat” in different spaces — Hindi classics alone, Eminem in a crowd. Not fake. Just adaptive. Because sometimes the door opens for the vibe first. <p>The post Eat dear Kanye, Eat dear Eminem first appeared on Her Campus.</p>

item.title: You Pinky Promise?
item.description: Adults didn’t really hold the best place in my heart. To me, they felt like old people who never really listen to anyone younger than them and here was a 50-year-old man actually promising me something and living up to it. A thing that adults find so easy to ignore. That was when I knew pinky promises really did mean something. <p>The post You Pinky Promise? first appeared on Her Campus.</p>
